thread:
emily: Quick riff  we need a refresh on the competitive battlecard for the launch week. Focus areas: short inbound hooks, webinar narrative, A/B messaging for field, and two tight rebut lines per competitor. Keep it skimmable for SDRs.
ryan: Can we avoid heavy benchmark claims in the top-line copy? Sales wants punchy bullets but legal flagged hard ratios. Use 'typical customers' and 'normalized benchmarks'.
maya: Draft hooks for inbound (30 char max):
- "Predictable inference spend"
- "From dev API to production SLOs"
- "No more inference firefights"
pavel: One-liners vs competitors:
- Cloud AI: "Managed models, uncertain tails  we guarantee serving economics."
- LLM APIs: "Easy to try, expensive to scale  we add predictable routing + fallbacks."
- Infra vendors: "You host, we operate inference as a product."
nina: Sanitzed benchmark blurb for the card (use as a callout):
"Normalized bench (16-token avg): p50 11ms Redwood, p50 33ms public API; normalized token cost: Redwood $0.00075 vs public $0.0020. Results vary by workload."
emily: Good. Also need two rebut scripts per competitor (one short, one extended). Keep short = 1 line, extended = 2 lines max.
ryan: Rebuts - Cloud AI:
- Short: "Scale doesn't mean predictable billing."
- Extended: "Their endpoints can introduce retries and cold starts that inflate unit cost; our reserved serving gives steady unit economics and SLOs."
maya: Rebuts - LLM APIs:
- Short: "APIs are great for PoCs; production needs guarantees."
- Extended: "We keep the dev ergonomics of an API while adding deterministic routing, autoscaling, and transparent unit-cost visibility."
pavel: Rebuts - Infra vendors:
- Short: "Hosting is not the same as running inference reliably."
- Extended: "Self-hosted stacks incur ongoing ops drain. We provide a packaged serving product (SLOs, KV caching, fallbacks) so teams ship features, not ops."
nina: Webinar angle: "Benchmarks, tradeoffs, and a live demo: real-time fallback from a busy region." Include 10 min Q&A with SE.
emily: Action items:
- @nina: paste the sanitized CSV + 1-paragraph methods note in the doc by EOD
- @pavel: produce the two rebut variants in the sales swipe file by tomorrow
- @ryan + @maya: draft webinar landing + 3 bullet agenda (hook, benchmark, playbook) by Thurs
- @emily: consolidate SDR 30s intros and push to #sales by Friday

deploy-bot: doc updated: /s/launch-battlecard-refresh v2 (emily) :white_check_mark:
emily: Reminder: language guardrails  use "predictable unit economics" and "ops cost reduction" instead of claiming "cheaper". Also include the caveat: "Benchmarks normalized to 16-token avg and steady-state batching; results vary by workload."
ryan: I'll run a quick field test with two reps tomorrow morning and report back.
maya: I'll mock the single-slide visual (callout + micro-bullets) and share.
emily: Thanks team  this should be different enough from the Q2 deck. We'll iterate after rep feedback.
